title: `make build` can link a stale shared XCFramework
reasoning: The build target only requires the XCFramework directory to exist. The directory target has no prerequisites on the shared/KMP sources or Gradle inputs, so after shared code changes `make build` will skip rebuilding the XCFramework and run `tuist build` against whatever binary was already present. That can produce an iOS build from stale shared code, which is a release/build correctness hazard.
reproduction: Build once to create `../shared/build/XCFrameworks/debug/EpilogueShared.xcframework`, modify shared code, then run `make -n build`; because the directory already exists, the dry run does not include `:shared:assembleEpilogueSharedXCFramework`.
recommendation: Make `build` and screenshot flows depend on the phony `xcframework` target when correctness matters, or model a real stamp/output file with source/input prerequisites so Make knows when the XCFramework is stale.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or CI smoke checks were provided for Makefile dependency behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Makefile smoke check or CI dry-run that verifies `make build` rebuilds or explicitly validates the XCFramework freshness after shared-source changes.
minimumFixScope: Update the Makefile dependencies for `build` and any release/screenshot target that must not consume a stale XCFramework.
